message.content:
In Blackjack, an **Ace** is special because it can be counted as **either 1 or 11 points**, depending on which value gives your hand the best advantage without causing a bust.

Key points:

| Situation | How the Ace is valued |
|-----------|-----------------------|
| You have a single Ace and the rest of your cards total ≤10 | Count the Ace as 11 (a “soft” hand). |
| Counting the Ace as 11 would make your total >21 | Count the Ace as 1 instead. |
| You have two Aces | One Ace is usually counted as 11 and the other as 1, giving a total of 12. If you hit and draw a low card, you may still treat one Ace as 11 while the other remains 1. |
| You have three or more Aces | Only one Ace can be counted as 11 at most; the others are counted as 1. |

So the Ace’s value is flexible: it always takes the value that keeps your hand from busting while maximizing its total. This flexibility is why hands containing an Ace are called “soft” hands (e.g., Ace‑7 = soft 18).

We should answer: Ace can count as either 1 or 11, whichever benefits the hand without busting; if counting as 11 would cause bust, it counts as 1. Also mention that if you have two Aces, one counts as 11 and the other as 1 unless both counted as 1 to avoid bust. Also mention that Ace can be used as a soft hand. So answer accordingly.
